title: Payment API returning HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
symptoms: API responds with HTTP 500 Internal Server Error
Failed or declined transactions at checkout
Spike in server-side errors on the API dashboard
possible_causes: Unhandled exception in application code
Payment gateway or downstream dependency unavailable
Database unavailable or connection pool exhausted
Faulty recent deployment
Missing or wrong environment variables / API credentials
diagnostic_checks: Review application logs for HTTP 500 errors and the stack trace around the failure time
Check dependencies: verify connectivity to the payment gateway (health endpoint, firewall rules, gateway status page)
Check the database dependency: availability and connection pool usage
Review API deployments made shortly before the errors started
Verify environment variables and API credentials are present and valid (do not paste secrets into tickets)
resolution: Inspect logs, dependencies and API configuration to find the failing component
Fix or roll back the faulty deployment if the errors began after a release
Restore the failed dependency (gateway or database) or fail over to a healthy instance
Correct the configuration or rotate expired credentials through the secrets manager
Re-run failed transactions only after the fix is confirmed

title: API returning HTTP 404 Not Found
symptoms: Requests return HTTP 404 Not Found
Endpoint worked previously but is now missing
Client integration reports resource not found
possible_causes: Wrong endpoint URL, path or API version in the request
Route removed or renamed in a recent release
Reverse proxy / API gateway routing misconfiguration
Requested record ID does not exist
diagnostic_checks: Compare the requested URL, HTTP method and API version against the current API documentation
Check the API gateway or reverse proxy (NGINX, ALB) routing rules for the path
Review recent releases for removed or renamed routes
Confirm the requested resource ID exists in the system
resolution: Update the client to the correct endpoint and API version
Restore or correct the gateway / proxy route
Re-deploy the missing route if it was removed by mistake

title: API request timeout
symptoms: API calls hang and fail with timeout errors
HTTP 504 Gateway Timeout from load balancer or proxy
Intermittent slow responses under load
possible_causes: Slow downstream service or third-party dependency
Long-running database queries
Server resource saturation (CPU, memory, thread pool)
Timeout values set too low on client, proxy or load balancer
diagnostic_checks: Check API latency metrics (p95 / p99) and the time the timeouts started
Trace a slow request end-to-end to find the slow dependency
Check database slow-query logs for queries triggered by the endpoint
Check CPU, memory and worker/thread pool usage on the API servers
Compare timeout settings across client, proxy, load balancer and application
resolution: Optimise or cache the slow dependency call
Scale out the API service if resources are saturated
Align timeout and retry settings across all layers
Add circuit breakers for unreliable third-party calls

title: API returning HTTP 401 / 403 authorization errors
symptoms: Requests rejected with HTTP 401 Unauthorized or 403 Forbidden
Integration stopped working without code changes
Token or API key reported as invalid or expired
possible_causes: Expired or revoked access token / API key
Missing Authorization header
Insufficient scopes or role permissions
Clock skew invalidating signed tokens
diagnostic_checks: Confirm the request includes the Authorization header (inspect headers, never share the key value)
Check token expiry and whether the key was rotated or revoked
Verify the client's scopes / roles allow the requested operation
Check server and client clock synchronisation (NTP)
resolution: Issue a new token or rotate the API key through the approved secrets process
Grant the correct scope or role following the access-request process
Fix NTP synchronisation if clock skew is found

title: Server unavailable / down
symptoms: Server cannot be reached by ping or SSH / RDP
Hosted services and websites are offline
Monitoring shows host down alert
possible_causes: Server powered off, crashed or rebooting
Hypervisor or cloud instance failure
Network or firewall change blocking access
Planned maintenance window
diagnostic_checks: Check monitoring and the cloud / hypervisor console for instance state
Ping the server and test SSH / RDP from another host on the same network
Check the change calendar for maintenance or recent firewall changes
Review console output or system logs for kernel panic / blue screen
resolution: Power on or restart the instance from the console if it is stopped
Revert the network or firewall change if access was blocked
Fail over to a standby server if the host has a hardware fault

title: High CPU utilization on server
symptoms: CPU usage consistently above 90%
Slow response from applications on the server
High load average alerts
possible_causes: Runaway or stuck process
Traffic spike beyond capacity
Inefficient code or infinite loop after a release
Malware or crypto-mining process
diagnostic_checks: Identify the top CPU-consuming processes (top / htop / Task Manager)
Correlate the CPU spike with traffic, cron jobs and recent deployments
Check for unknown or suspicious processes
Review CPU trend graphs to tell a spike from sustained growth
resolution: Restart or kill the runaway process after confirming it is safe to do so
Scale up or scale out to handle the higher load
Roll back the release if it introduced inefficient code
Report suspicious processes to the security team

title: Server not responding / hung
symptoms: Server responds to ping but services do not respond
SSH / RDP sessions freeze or are very slow
Requests queue up and eventually fail
possible_causes: Memory exhaustion and heavy swapping
Disk I/O saturation
Deadlocked or hung service process
File descriptor or connection limit reached
diagnostic_checks: Check memory and swap usage (free -m, vmstat) and OOM-killer messages
Check disk I/O wait (iostat) and disk latency
Check whether the main service process is alive and accepting connections
Check open file descriptors and connection counts against limits
resolution: Restart the hung service, then the server if the service restart fails
Add memory or fix the memory-hungry process
Raise file descriptor / connection limits if they were reached

title: Server disk space full
symptoms: 'No space left on device' errors
Applications fail to write logs or files
Disk usage alert above 90%
possible_causes: Log files growing without rotation
Old backups or temp files not cleaned up
Large core dumps
Unexpected data growth
diagnostic_checks: Check filesystem usage (df -h) and find the largest directories (du -sh)
Check log rotation configuration
Look for old backups, temp files and core dumps
Check inode usage (df -i)
resolution: Archive or delete old logs and temp files following the retention policy
Fix or enable log rotation
Expand the volume if the growth is legitimate

title: Database connection failure
symptoms: Application errors such as 'could not connect to server' or 'connection refused'
Connection pool exhausted errors
Application pages fail to load data
possible_causes: Database service stopped or crashed
Network / firewall / security group blocking the database port
Maximum connections limit reached
Wrong host, port or database name in configuration
diagnostic_checks: Check whether the database service is running and accepting connections
Test connectivity to the database host and port from the application server (telnet / nc)
Check current connection count against the max_connections limit
Verify host, port and database name in the application configuration
resolution: Start or fail over the database service
Fix the firewall / security group rule for the database port
Tune the connection pool or kill idle connections
Correct the connection string configuration

title: Database query timeout
symptoms: Queries fail with timeout or 'statement cancelled' errors
Reports or pages that run heavy queries load slowly
Database CPU or I/O spikes
possible_causes: Missing or unused index
Locking or blocking by another transaction
Outdated table statistics producing a bad query plan
Large data growth on the queried tables
diagnostic_checks: Find the slow query in the slow-query log or query store
Run EXPLAIN / execution plan to check for full table scans
Check for blocking sessions and long-running transactions
Check when table statistics were last updated
resolution: Add or fix the index the query needs
Resolve the blocking transaction
Update statistics and rebuild fragmented indexes
Rewrite or paginate the heavy query

title: Database authentication failure
symptoms: 'Access denied for user' or 'password authentication failed' errors
Application cannot log in to the database after a change
Locked database account
possible_causes: Database password changed or expired
Account locked after repeated failed attempts
User lacks grants on the database or schema
Connecting host not allowed by access rules (pg_hba.conf, host grants)
diagnostic_checks: Check database logs for the exact authentication error
Check whether the account is locked or its password has expired
Verify the user's grants on the target database and schema
Check host-based access rules for the application server's IP
resolution: Reset or rotate the credential through the secrets manager and update the application
Unlock the account after finding the source of the failed attempts
Grant the missing privileges following the access-request process

title: Database deadlocks
symptoms: 'Deadlock detected' or 'deadlock victim' errors
Intermittent failed transactions under concurrent load
Retries succeed after a failure
possible_causes: Transactions locking tables or rows in different orders
Long transactions holding locks
Missing indexes causing wider locks
diagnostic_checks: Capture the deadlock graph / report from the database
Identify the competing queries and their lock order
Check transaction duration for the affected operations
resolution: Make transactions access objects in a consistent order
Shorten transactions and add retry logic for deadlock victims
Add indexes to narrow the locked range

title: Internet connectivity failure
symptoms: No internet access from a workstation or office
Browser shows 'No internet' or 'ERR_INTERNET_DISCONNECTED'
Internal resources may still be reachable
possible_causes: Cable unplugged, Wi-Fi disconnected or NIC disabled
No IP address from DHCP (169.254.x.x address)
Default gateway, router or firewall failure
ISP outage
diagnostic_checks: Check physical connection or Wi-Fi status and that the network adapter is enabled
Run ipconfig / ip addr to confirm a valid IP address and default gateway
Ping the default gateway, then a public IP such as 8.8.8.8
Check whether other users at the same site are affected and check the ISP status
resolution: Reconnect the cable / Wi-Fi or re-enable the adapter
Renew the DHCP lease (ipconfig /release and /renew)
Restart or fail over the router / firewall
Raise a ticket with the ISP for a confirmed outage

title: DNS resolution failure
symptoms: Websites fail with 'DNS_PROBE_FINISHED_NXDOMAIN' or 'could not resolve host'
Sites work by IP address but not by name
Internal hostnames do not resolve
possible_causes: DNS server unreachable or down
Wrong DNS server configured on the client
Missing or wrong DNS record
Stale DNS cache
diagnostic_checks: Run nslookup / dig against the configured DNS server
Compare resolution with a known good DNS server
Confirm the DNS server settings on the client or DHCP scope
Check the DNS record in the zone for the failing hostname
resolution: Flush the DNS cache (ipconfig /flushdns)
Correct the DNS server settings
Restore the DNS service or fix the missing record

title: VPN connection problem
symptoms: VPN client fails to connect or disconnects frequently
Connected to VPN but cannot reach internal resources
VPN authentication or certificate errors
possible_causes: Expired credentials, MFA failure or expired certificate
Outdated VPN client version
Local firewall or home network blocking VPN ports
VPN gateway overloaded or down
Split-tunnel or route configuration issue
diagnostic_checks: Confirm the user's account and MFA work for other company services
Check the VPN client version and its log for the exact error
Check internet connectivity without VPN and try another network
Check VPN gateway status and concurrent session count
If connected but resources are unreachable, check routes and DNS over the tunnel
resolution: Reset credentials / re-enrol MFA or renew the client certificate
Update or reinstall the VPN client
Allow the VPN ports on the local firewall or use another network
Escalate gateway capacity or outage to the network team

title: Slow network / high latency and packet loss
symptoms: Slow file transfers and lagging video calls
High ping times or packet loss
Problems limited to a site, floor or Wi-Fi area
possible_causes: Link saturation by large transfers or backups
Faulty cable, switch port or access point
Wi-Fi interference or weak signal
ISP congestion
diagnostic_checks: Run ping and traceroute / pathping to find where latency or loss starts
Check bandwidth utilisation on the uplink
Check switch port errors and access point health
Test wired vs wireless to isolate Wi-Fi problems
resolution: Reschedule or throttle large transfers
Replace the faulty cable / port or move the user to a healthy access point
Apply QoS for voice and video traffic
Raise a ticket with the ISP for upstream congestion

title: User login failure in application
symptoms: User cannot log in to the application
'Invalid username or password' or 'account locked' message
Single sign-on (SSO) redirect loop or error
possible_causes: Wrong or expired password
Account locked or disabled
SSO / identity provider issue or certificate expiry
User not assigned to the application
diagnostic_checks: Confirm whether one user or many users are affected
Check the account status (locked, disabled, password expired) in the directory
Check the identity provider / SSO status and sign-in logs
Confirm the user is assigned the application role or group
Ask the user to try a private browser window to rule out cached sessions
resolution: Unlock the account or start a password reset through the self-service portal (never ask for the password)
Assign the missing application role or group
Escalate SSO / identity provider failures affecting many users

title: Application crash
symptoms: Application closes unexpectedly or shows a crash dialog
Service restarts repeatedly (crash loop)
Error reports or crash dumps generated
possible_causes: Bug triggered by specific input or action
Out-of-memory condition
Corrupt installation, cache or configuration
Incompatible update or missing dependency
diagnostic_checks: Collect the steps to reproduce and the exact time of the crash
Check application logs, Windows Event Viewer or crash dumps
Check memory usage before the crash
Check for recent application, OS or dependency updates
resolution: Clear the application cache or reset its configuration
Repair or reinstall the application
Roll back the incompatible update
Send logs and reproduction steps to the application support team for a code fix

title: Slow application performance
symptoms: Pages or screens take a long time to load
Users report the application is running slowly
Increased response times on monitoring
possible_causes: Slow database queries
Server resource saturation
Network latency between user and application
Large client-side cache or too much data loaded at once
Recent release with a performance regression
diagnostic_checks: Confirm whether the slowness affects one user, one site or all users
Check application response time and error rate on monitoring / APM
Check server CPU, memory and disk usage
Check database slow-query logs
Compare performance before and after the latest release
resolution: Optimise the slow queries or add caching
Scale the application servers
Clear the client cache for single-user issues
Roll back the release that caused the regression

title: SSL/TLS certificate expired or invalid
symptoms: Browser shows 'Your connection is not private' or certificate warning
API clients fail with SSL handshake or certificate verify errors
Errors begin on a specific date
possible_causes: Certificate expired
Hostname not covered by the certificate
Incomplete certificate chain (missing intermediate)
Client trusts an outdated root store
diagnostic_checks: Check the certificate expiry date and hostnames (openssl s_client or browser details)
Verify the full chain including intermediate certificates
Confirm which servers / load balancers serve the certificate
resolution: Renew and install the certificate on every server / load balancer that serves it
Install the missing intermediate certificate
Set up automatic renewal and expiry monitoring
